author: haiku
label: c2-seed-haiku-01
changes: Removed the Evaluator-to-IncidentManager breach message. Evaluators now write each minute's result to Postgres, and the incident manager is involved only when an incident opens.
Added the evaluation-row claim so exactly one evaluator handles each minute, with the streak update in the same transaction.
Added a unique index and open-incident pointer so only one unresolved incident exists per service and rule, and breaches during an open incident are counted without paging.

Defined the timer queue and the escalate message: queued 5 minutes after each primary or secondary page, carrying incident id and level, and a no-op if the incident is acked, resolved or at a different level.
Added the incident.level column (0 primary, 1 secondary, 2 EM) and the schedule lookup at page time, so the 09:00 handover is respected.
Defined the ack and escalate race through one row lock on the incident, and the ack webhook lookup through page_log.

Defined the push-then-SMS fallback as the incident manager's decision, with a 10-second push timeout (my choice, flagged as an open question), and the rule that the escalate clock starts when the page is sent regardless of result.
Defined page_log as one row per page attempt, written only by the incident manager, and separated it from the incident table.

Added the full set of brief rules that were missing: 500-request minimum, 1% clear rule with 10-minute streak, resolved notice to everyone paged, resolve-before-ack stopping escalation, and the rule that no timer follows the EM page.

Replaced the Notes list with a summary, terms, the diagram, rules the diagram does not show, a failure table and open questions, so each fact appears once. The file is longer than the first version because the brief's stated rules had to be kept.
The junior-dev loop was not run in this round: no tools were available, so the teach-back did not run.
Summary rewritten to say how the evaluator, incident manager and Postgres fit together, and why only the winning evaluator acts on a minute (Q9).

Terms: added incident manager (a module the evaluator calls after commit, plus timer and webhook callers), row lock, provider reference, neither, and the trailing-rate definition from the metrics store (Q9, Q10, Q12).

Diagram: the evaluator calls the incident manager after commit (Q9). Each page logs its attempts, and escalate checks the level it was paged at (Q15). The ack path looks up the incident from page_log before taking the lock (Q12).
Rule 1: a window with no requests, or no series, changes nothing, and the reason is given (Q10).
Rule 5: resolved notices go to each paged person, once (Q11).
Rule 6: added the page content and the failed-lookup handling, and the provider reference is stored per attempt (Q12, Q13, Q16).
Rule 8: defined the stale check and what the escalate message's level means (Q15).
Rule 9: stated that an ack does not change breach counting or resolving (Q14).
Rule 11: resolved notices are one per distinct person, levels never reached get none, and timers that fire later do nothing (Q11).
Removed references to numbered rules inside the text, so each step stands alone.
Failure table: split the schedule-lookup case, added the push-delivered-but-timed-out case, duplicate escalate, and resolved-notice failure.
Open questions: added the timed-out push ack matching gap (Q12) and the unset page wording (Q16).
Cut the repeated flow: the opening paragraph now gives the main flow once, and the rules add only what the diagram cannot show.
Merged the two streak-reset statements into rule 1, and the separate 'every page' and 'lookup failed' explanations into the single page procedure in rule 6.
Moved the Postgres table descriptions out of Terms into one 'Where state lives' section, so each table is defined once.
Added one-line definitions for 5xx, alert rule, escalation level numbers (0, 1, 2), row lock, and the webhook as an address the provider calls.
Put the failure handling into one table and kept all 13 rows from the first version.

Kept every fact from the brief and first version: 60-second cycle, 5-minute trailing window, 2% and 500-request breach test, 1% clear test, 3-breach opening, 10 quiet minutes to resolve, 5-minute escalation steps, EM as last level, push then SMS with a 10-second timeout, 09:00 handover, one incident per service and rule, one resolved notice per person, and all five open questions.
Kept the Mermaid sequence diagram unchanged in form and content; the notes follow it as the skill requires.
Kept the answers' decisions as stated: ack stops escalation only, breaches still count after an ack, a failed lookup pages nobody at that level, and the escalate check's stale rule.
